Installing Widget

Widget runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. It needs Python 3.10 or newer and about 40 MB of disk space. The steps below install the command-line tool and the Python library together.

Requirements

Check your Python version first. Widget is tested on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, and older versions are not supported because the parser relies on newer typing features.

  • Python 3.10 or newer
  • pip 23 or newer
  • A C compiler is not required

Install with pip

Create a virtual environment so Widget's dependencies stay separate from the rest of your system, then install the package from PyPI.

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install widget

Run widget --version to confirm the install worked. You should see the version number printed on one line.

Upgrading

To move to the newest release, run pip again with the upgrade flag. Your configuration file is kept.

pip install --upgrade widget

Troubleshooting

If the install fails with a permissions error you are probably outside the virtual environment. Activate it again and repeat the command; never install Widget with sudo.

ErrorFix
Permission deniedActivate the virtual environment
No matching distributionUpgrade pip, then retry
